newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt fiscal 96/97 revenue seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt fiscal 96/97 revenue seen falling.

text.p: Deputy finance minister Chaturon Chaisaeng said on Thursday that Thai government revenue for fiscal 1996/97 (October-September) is expected to be 880 billion baht ($33.8 billion) against an earlier projected 925 billion.

"The finance ministry has revised down government revenue for this fiscal year. The revenue is expected to be at 880 billion baht compared with a previous forecast of 925 billion baht," Chaturon told reporters.
The finance ministry's permanent secretary Chatumongkol Sonakul said the government would not cut its spending further as a result of the lower-than-expected revenue.
"Any additional reduction in government spending might further hurt the economy," he said.
The government early this year cut its projection of expected revenue to about 925 billion baht from a previous projection of 984 billion baht.

A slowdown in the Thai economy, which has been plagued by troubles in the financial and property sectors, sluggish exports, a plunging stock market and a weak currency, is seen by analysts as the reason for the low tax and revenue collection.
"However, the government's spending and revenue is expected to remained balanced this year," Chatumongkol said, indicating that there would be no deficit budget.
